ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the vertex $P$ of a $30^\circ$ angle of a right-angled triangle board falls on the circle $\odot O$, and the two sides intersect the circle $\odot O$ at points $A$ and $B$, respectively. If $AO$ and $BO$ are connected, what is the degree measure of $\angle AOB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since $\angle P=30^\circ$, $\angle AOB=2\angle P$\\
Therefore, $\angle AOB=\boxed{60^\circ}$

From the text, model A, B, and P as points on the same circle centered at O, with chords PA and PB forming a 30° angle at P. Use an analytic derivation instead of directly quoting the inscribed-angle theorem: set the circle to have radius 1 and rotate coordinates so P = (1,0). The chord direction from P to a point with parameter t has vector (cos t − 1, sin t), whose line direction changes by half the change in t.
